title: Code Review is now generally available
summary: Claude Code's PR review feature is now generally available for Team and Enterprise organizations, and most reviews finish in 6-10 minutes, down from about 20 minutes in preview. Admins can set review depth per repo as Quick, Standard (the default), or Deep, and setup uses Claude Code settings plus a GitHub App, with reviews running automatically on new PRs. It targets review as the bottleneck now that coding agents speed up code creation.

title: Automating eval design and hillclimbing with Claude
summary: Claude Code adds two claude-api skill commands, /claude-api build-eval and /claude-api hillclimb. build-eval interviews the user, samples inputs, proposes the cheapest grader, and checks baseline headroom, while hillclimb patches one surface per round with a train/test split and reverts overfit or regressing patches. On a support benchmark, cost fell from 4.6c to 1c per ticket and held-out accuracy rose from 78.6% to 90.5%, with guardrails meant to make gains hold in production.

title: How Comcast and Booz Allen use Claude Mythos to find exploit chains and secure their codebases
summary: Security teams used Claude Mythos-class models through Project Glasswing, a limited-access program for critical infrastructure defenders. Comcast found a critical auth flaw across 258 systems and fixed it before exploitation, and a Booz Allen analyst reviewed 8 systems across 138 repos in 12 days, finding a pre-boot key weakness. The models trace exploit chains across code, config, identity, and deployment that single-file scanners miss, and validating findings is now the bottleneck, with humans still confirming and routing.

title: Uber's CISO on building an insider threat program for AI
summary: Uber CISO Philip Martin describes an insider-threat program for AI agents that pairs Anthropic's Enterprise Frontier Safeguards with Uber's open-source AI Detection and Response (ADR) tool. ADR collects real-time agent telemetry, detects out-of-bounds behavior, and can intervene, while the Safeguards let Uber keep data control and decide responses to triggers. Martin argues that models need insider-risk monitoring just as employees do.

title: How an Anthropic Japan business development representative runs his day with a fleet of Claude agents
summary: BDR Shahboz Ibragimov runs his workday with six agents built on Claude Managed Agents (beta) and Claude Tag, which handle lead routing, email drafts, and CRM updates before his day starts. He estimates about 60 hours saved and moved his prototypes to Managed Agents for background scheduling, shared memory, and scoped credential vaults. The case shows a non-developer can build an agent fleet in plain language, with humans reviewing judgment calls.

title: Build live dashboards and animate explainers with Claude
summary: Anthropic introduced Dashboards, which turn plain-language questions into always-current charts connected to BigQuery, Databricks, Snowflake, and Salesforce (beta on paid plans), and Motion, which turns prompts into short animated explainers exportable as MP4 (beta on Team and Enterprise). Docs, Slides, and Design are now out of beta and available on all plans, including Free. Charts show their underlying query and animations are editable code, so results can be checked.
